h: Purity Within and Holiness Without in the Shabbos Cup

p: In the holy Zohar on this parshah
for the cup, which is Elohim Chaim, is Binah."
and Binah is the World to Come,
and this is why it says "Elohim Chaim, Binah."
we find among the Avos only with Yitzchak,
"And he brought him wine, and he drank";
although regarding Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
yet there it is not mentioned that he drank;
moreover, there it was a seudas mitzvah,
and it is stated in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer:
on the eighth day he circumcised";
"And make me tasty food such as I love";
and we said that his intent was
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַמְּכוּוָּן שֶׁל עֵשָׂו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
that Esav's intent be for the sake of Heaven,
to fulfill the mitzvah of honoring a parent;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִהְיֶה אֲכִילָתוֹ מִצְוָה
and thereby his eating would be a mitzvah,
the son fulfills the mitzvah of honoring,
along the lines of the reasoning of the Ran
(beginning of the second chapter of Kiddushin)
regarding a woman who assists her husband.
וּמִשּׁוּם הַאי טַעְמָא כְּתִיב (בְּרֵאשִׁית כה, כח)
And for this reason it is written (Bereishis 25:28):
וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו
"And Yitzchak loved Esav, for his game was in his mouth,"
"for he would eat of his game";
the taste of a seudas mitzvah of honoring
(and this was explained in parshas Toldos);
and with him the wine was
according to his attribute, the attribute of "the Fear of Yitzchak."
And this is why it says "with wine in the cup,"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
And the Ra'aya Mehemna says afterward:
that it requires rinsing and washing:
and the secret of the matter
is that his inside be like his outside, etc.;
and the secret of the matter:
'And he shall purify it and sanctify it' (Vayikra 16:19):
And from the expression "his inside like his outside"
it implies that his inside is superior to his outside,
Yet in truth "purity leads to holiness,"
so it appears that holiness is greater;
so why does it say purity within
But holiness is not at all holiness
except when it comes through purity,
that the heart first be purified
from "the heart of a fool, which is at his left";
and then the holiness is called holiness;
otherwise it is not holiness at all.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּפָרָשַׁת קֹרַח (בְּמִדְבַּר טז, ג)
And this is what is said in parshas Korach (Bamidbar 16:3):
"For the whole congregation are all holy,
and Hashem is in their midst";
that is, Hashem Yisbarach dwells in their heart,
and the whole holiness of Havayah,
which includes the upper and lower Shechinah,
and the yetzer hara has cleared out from there;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה כָּל הָעֵדָה כּוּלָּם קְדוֹשִׁים
and thereby "the whole congregation are all holy."
And this is why it says
that his inside be like his outside,
And it says: "And just as a cup,
there is no purifying and sanctifying of it
there is no purifying and sanctifying of it
That is, the purification from the yetzer hara
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
is only through words of Torah,
as is written in the holy Zohar
to break the yetzer hara except Torah";
הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
is only through words of Torah,
it is not within the category of holiness at all.
whoever's inside is not like his outside
shall not enter the beis midrash,
from the side of the Tree of Life
but from the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil."
הוּא רַק מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע
is only from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil,
prohibited and permitted, valid and invalid,
as is written in the holy Zohar
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
this means that through the Oral Torah,
אַף שֶׁהוּא מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע
although it is from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil,
so that it be only from the side of good,
מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע אִילָנָא דְּחַיֵּי
out of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil a Tree of Life;
and then his inside is like his outside.
And I heard that they asked:
to know whether one's inside is like his outside?
But this statement of Rabban Gamliel
"Any student whose inside is not like his outside
shall not enter the beis midrash,"
thereby one whose inside was not like his outside
וְלֹא הָיָה לוֹ חֵשֶׁק כְּלָל לִכְנוֹס
and he had no desire at all to enter.
"over which the Tree of Life rules,"
as is written in the holy Zohar
then every one of Yisrael merits
as they said in the Yerushalmi (Demai 4:1):
"The awe of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz";
and through keeping Shabbos we merit
that He makes a dwelling for them on Shabbos
in the two chambers of the heart,
and the yetzer hara clears out from there,
and then it leads to holiness,
and we merit a new soul,
that one's inside be like his outside;
and this is why we say "with wine in the cup."
